samples.summary: No test covers the new `requestLayoutRefresh` dirty-set save/restore, the only production change in editor.ts
samples.evidence: The delta rewrites `textEditor.requestLayoutRefresh` (editor.ts:2545-2549) so `dirtyBlockIds` survives the mid-unit layout pass. Every keystroke reaches it: typing runs through `TextEditor.withUndoUnit` (text-editor.ts:1020, 3840) and the held `requestRender` calls `requestLayoutRefresh()` (text-editor.ts:739), then the post-unit paint calls `render()` → `recomputeLayout()`. Without the restore, both passes run with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined`, i.e. `canUseCache` is false (layout.ts:457) and the WHOLE document is re-measured per keypress. Nothing asserts this. `packages/docs/test/view/cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts` already has the exact harness (40 blocks, a `measureText` counter on the OffscreenCanvas stub, `expect(measureTextCalls).toBeLessThan(40)`) but only exercises ArrowRight/ArrowDown — no input/typing case. `incremental-layout.test.ts` tests `computeLayout` in isolation and never goes through the editor or an undo unit, so it cannot see a dropped dirty set. A future revert to `requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout` reintroduces per-keystroke full re-layout (visible typing lag on long documents) with the suite still green.

samples.summary: Adding `readOnly` to the editor-init effect deps has no test: nothing pins that losing write authority re-initializes the editor
samples.evidence: The delta adds `readOnly` to the `useEffect` deps that call `initialize()` (docs-view.tsx:572), whose stated purpose is that a session demoted from `editor` to `viewer` no longer keeps a writable editor. I could find no test that renders `DocsView` at all: grepping `DocsView` in packages/frontend/tests matches only comments (docs-context-menu.test.tsx:170, docs-table-context-menu.test.tsx:134), and `grep docs-view` in the frontend test tree matches only two unrelated comments in yorkie-doc-store.test.ts. So neither the permission-enforcement behavior nor the remount it introduces (editor teardown/rebuild dropping caret + local undo history when the flag flips) is covered; a regression that drops the dep restores a silent write-after-demotion path with the suite green.

samples.summary: The new `readOnly` re-check in `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` is untested
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:4261 adds `this.readOnly` to the post-await guard of `pastePlainTextFromClipboard`. `packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts` covers `pasteFormat()` against the class (l.576-681) and the store/doc handles, but has no Cmd+Shift+V / `readText()` case; `large-paste-indicator.test.ts` stubs `navigator.clipboard.readText` for the HTML paste path only, and the new frontend test in editor-undo-selection.test.ts exercises plain paste with a writable editor. So the guard could be deleted without any failure. Impact is contained today because `readOnly` is fixed at construction (l.191/719) and the keydown gate at l.1096 already blocks the shortcut, which is why this is minor rather than major — but the guard is the stated defence for a mid-prompt permission change and nothing pins it.

samples.summary: 'insertText over a multi-block selection is one undo unit' passes even if no selection existed — its own assertions don't establish the multi-block precondition
samples.evidence: The test dispatches Cmd/Ctrl+A and then asserts `watch.outermost() === 1`, `writesOutsideABatch() === 0`, and that undo restores `['alpha','beta']`. If the select-all had not taken effect (e.g. the keydown never reached `TextEditor.handleKeyDown`, or `selectAll()` early-returned), `insertText('X')` would be a plain caret insert: still exactly one outermost `batch()` (`TextEditor.insertText` → `withUndoUnit`, text-editor.ts:828-835), no escaped writes, and undo would still restore `['alpha','beta']`. So all three assertions hold with the precondition absent, and the scenario named in the title is only actually established by the sibling test ('insertText really writes what it was given', which asserts `['X']`). Asserting the replaced text (or the selection) inside this test would make it self-contained; as written the coverage claim depends on a second test that could be edited or skipped independently.

samples.summary: `writesOutsideABatch()` watches only a partial allowlist of store writes, so a `0` can be vacuous
samples.evidence: `writeNames` (l.890-893) covers 9 of MemDocStore's mutators and omits others the delete/insert paths can reach (`insertBlocksAfter`, `applyStyle`/`applyStyles`, `setBlockType`, `applyBlockStyle`, `insertImageInline`, `updateTableCell`, …; see packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:93,361,367,393,429,470). A write escaping the unit through an unwatched method would leave the counter at 0, so the 'no write escapes' assertion is weaker than it reads. The neighbouring `outermost() === 1` assertion still carries the test, hence nit.

verdict.reason: The production seam exists (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2545-2549, called from packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:735-740), and nothing tests it. A repo-wide grep for `requestLayoutRefresh|layoutRefresh` over *.test.ts returns zero files. All three `dirtyBlockIds` test hits are off-path: incremental-layout.test.ts:24-57 and char-offsets-cache.test.ts:45-59 call `computeLayout` directly with hand-built dirty sets and never mount an editor; cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts:121-138 mounts the real editor with a counting measureText stub but only presses ArrowRight/ArrowDown, so it never opens an undo unit. I checked every indirect observer I could find: the only other measurement counter in the repo is font-load-invalidation.test.ts:19 (font-load events, not typing), and packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts does type through a real withUndoUnit (line 329-333) but counts only ctx.save/paint (line 363-372) with an uncounted measureText stub (line 49-54), so a dropped dirty set cannot make it fail. editor.ts exposes no layout/dirty-set test hook (only _setSelectionForTest/_setEditContextForTest/_getCursorForTest), and there is no bench/perf suite. So a revert to `requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout` would keep the suite green while restoring a per-keystroke full re-layout.

verdict.reason: Verified the change and the absence. docs-view.tsx:581 lists `readOnly` in the deps of the editor-init effect (with react-hooks/exhaustive-deps disabled on the same line), and the effect's `initialize(container, store, theme, readOnly)` at line 359 plus `editor.dispose()` teardown at line 565 is, per the in-code comment at 572-580, "the only place that permission is applied". No test anywhere in the repo imports or renders DocsView: a repo-wide grep for `DocsView|docs-view` matches only source, task docs, and comments inside unrelated tests (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:598,644; copy-integrity.test.ts:560,629; editor-read-only.test.ts:871). The only importer of the module, docs-detail.tsx:27, is itself imported by no test. Adjacent candidates cover different layers and would all pass with the dep removed: docs-find-bar-read-only.test.tsx:64,82,98 passes readOnly to the find bar (never flipping it on a mounted tree), and packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts (lines 107-931) pins enforcement given an already read-only initialize, not the rebuild-on-flip. No e2e/playwright suite exists and no rerender/setProps test touches DocsView, so nothing pins that losing write authority re-initializes the editor; because exhaustive-deps is suppressed there, lint would not catch the regression either. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a behavior change that silently weakens a write guard with no meaningful test = major.

finding.summary: Hangul commit-over-a-selection now wrapped in `withUndoUnit`, but no test covers the selection-replacement Hangul path
finding.evidence: `applyHangulResult` wraps `deleteSelection()` + `docInsertText()` in `withUndoUnit` (text-editor.ts:5891). This is the same #1045 shape (delete N blocks, then write) for Korean typing over a select-all, so losing the unit reproduces the same unrecoverable-tail data loss the diff exists to fix. hangul.test.ts only exercises `HangulAssembler` directly (no editor, no selection); ime-composition-editor.test.ts documents that it cannot assert Yorkie undo-unit counts; text-box-composing.test.ts is the slides text-box preview. No test in docs or frontend types a jamo over a non-empty selection and counts undo units.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is false: a test that types a jamo over a non-empty select-all and counts undo units exists in the very file the reviewer reports as empty. editor-undo-selection.test.ts:448-459 ("a Hangul commit over a select-all is one undo unit") calls selectAll() across a 100-paragraph document (PARAGRAPHS=100 at line 284; selectAll spans block[0] offset 0 to the last block's end, lines 317-327), then type('ㄳ'), which sets textarea.value and dispatches a real input event (lines 329-333). I traced that this reaches the code under review: text-editor.ts:999-1008 routes single-char jamo through isJamo -> hangulAssembler.feed -> applyHangulResult, and hangul.ts:135-138 returns a commit with no composing for a code absent from LEAD (ㄳ is a compound consonant), so with hangulComposingText === '' execution lands exactly on the withUndoUnit(() => { deleteSelection(); docInsertText(...) }) branch at text-editor.ts:5895-5901 that the finding names. The test is neither vacuous nor over-mocked: it uses a real yorkie.Document, a real YorkieDocStore and real initialize() (lines 292-306), asserts the write actually landed (expect(texts().join('')).toBe('ㄳ')) to exclude an empty-unit pass, asserts the undo-unit count equals before + 1 read from the real doc.getUndoStackForTest(), and asserts one undo restores all 100 paragraphs. The document is deliberately sized above Yorkie's 50-entry cap so a dropped unit fails loudly. A companion test at lines 461-472 covers the lead-jamo half where only the selection delete reaches the store. The file's doc comment at lines 432-447 names applyHangulResult at line 439, so even a plain repo-wide grep surfaces this coverage.
